text: これ　たのまれてるんだけど　わたして　くれるかい！

structure.jp: たのまれてるんだけど
structure.en: I've been asked to handle it, but

structure.jp: わたして　くれるかい！
structure.en: will you hand it over for me?

patterns.name: 〜られる (passive)
patterns.explanation: The れ in the verb shows the thing was done to the speaker. てる is a shortened ている. たのまれてる = 'I've been asked'.

patterns.name: 〜てくれる
patterns.explanation: くれる after a て-verb means someone does it as a favour for the speaker. わたして　くれる = 'hand it over for me'.

patterns.name: 〜のだ
patterns.explanation: んだ adds a feeling of explaining the situation, and けど after it leads softly into the request. たのまれてるんだ = 'the thing is, I've been asked'.
